protocol.py: 4 biology problems (1 error, 1 warning, 2 notes).

1. ERROR PIPETTE-RANGE: 2.38 ul, 2.63 ul, 2.86 ul, 3.33 ul and 19 more are below what the
p300_single_gen2 can measure (20 ul at least)
   line 69:  p300.aspirate(sample_ul, src_well)
   At line 69 the p300_single_gen2 is asked to draw 2.38 ul, 2.63 ul, 2.86 ul, 3.33 ul and
   19 more, below its minimum of 20 ul (this line did it 23 times). A pipette cannot measure
   less than its minimum: it draws the wrong amount, or nothing, and the volumes in this
   protocol only add up on paper. The simulator passes the move. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3,
   B1, B2, C1, C2, C3 and 15 more in slot 2.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, B1, B2, C1, C2, C3 and 15 more in slot 2.
   Fix: Use a pipette whose range covers the volume (a p20 for 1 to 20 ul), or scale the
   reaction so every volume is at least the pipette's minimum.
   Source: Opentrons: pipette characteristics (volume ranges)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/pipettes/characteristics.html
   Source: Integra: pipetting tips (work at 35 to 100% of nominal volume)
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/united-states/en/pipetting-tips
   [02a17a5b60ac]

2. WARNING MIX-TOO-WEAK: Mixing too weak to stir 24 wells: 3 × 25 ul in 50 ul
   line 71:  p300.mix(3, 25, dst_well)  # optional mixing
   At line 71 the tip mixes wells A1, A2, A3, B1, B2, B3, C1, C2 and 16 more in slot 3 with
   3 strokes of 25 ul in a well holding 50 ul (this line did it 24 times). 3 strokes of 25
   ul move 1.5 of the well in all; it takes about 2 wells' worth of strokes to mix (the
   mixing work). Integra draws over 80% of the well five times; three mixes gave 11.8% CV
   where twenty gave 1.7%. What the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated,
   and in a dilution series every later step inherits the error.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, B1, B2, B3, C1, C2 and 16 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Mix the well with about 80% of its volume (40 ul) at least 5 times: `mix(5, 40,
   well)`. A stroke of the whole well draws air; use no more than 90%.
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   Source: Integra: three serial-dilution protocols (over 80% of the volume, five times)
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applications/3-simple-and-proven-automation-protocols-serial-dilutions-assist-plus-pipetting-robot
   Source: Beckman AMPure XP instructions (mix with a tip volume just below the well volume)
           https://research.fredhutch.org/content/dam/research/hahn/methods/Agencourt%20AMPure%20XP.pdf
   Source: Esca Automation: serial dilution, a classic technique
           https://escaautomation.substack.com/p/serial-dilution-a-classic-technique
   Source: labautomation.io 3654: how to mix a bacteria sample enough
           https://labautomation.io/t/how-to-mix-bacteria-sample-enough/3654
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   [771d58100609]

3. NOTE WELL-CAPACITY: Declared more than the well holds: 20000 ul in a 15015 ul well, 1
well
   line 68:  p300.aspirate(water_ul, reservoir_well)
   At line 68 the robot draws from well A1 in slot 4, which the protocol declares (line 37)
   to hold 20000 ul; the well holds 15014.5 ul. The prep sheet cannot be followed as
   written. Wells: well A1 in slot 4.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 4.
   Fix: Declare what the well can really hold, or use a bigger container.
   Source: Opentrons labware schema 2: totalLiquidVolume, the total well volume in
   microlitres
           https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Opentrons/opentrons/edge/shared-data/labware/schemas/2.json
   Source: Bartley et al. 2023, LabOP: a protocol never adds more liquid than its container
   holds
           https://jakebeal.github.io/Publications/JETC23-LabOP.pdf
   [39ba0d4f6ecb]

4. NOTE CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: 24 stocks
   line 69:  p300.aspirate(sample_ul, src_well)
   At line 69 the tip went into sample 1 (well A1 in slot 2), sample 9 (well A2 in slot 2),
   sample 17 (well A3 in slot 2), sample 2 (well B1 in slot 2) and 20 more while it still
   carried water (well A1 in slot 4) from an earlier step (this line did it 24 times). A tip
   that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so these
   stocks now hold material that does not belong there. The protocol does not draw from them
   again, so this run is not harmed, but what is left in the stock is no longer clean for
   the next run.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, B1, B2, B3, C1, C2 and 16 more in slot 2.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 69 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [5c14c4a7bf4a]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.
